messages.subject: replot detection function in MCDS
parts:
Dear all,

I'm estimating brown hares' densities using distance sampling point transect in France.
I used 2 covariates for the detection function : site and year. 
My best fitted model is:
final <- ds(dataDS,transect="point",formula=~CovYear+zone,
            key="hn",adjustment="herm",order=2,cutpoints=c(0,220,320,420,560,600),convert.units=0.001)
here is the summary of the model:
Summary for distance analysis
Number of observations :  10897
Distance range         :  0  -  600


Model : Half-normal key function with Hermite polynomial adjustment term of order 4
AIC   : 19897.87


Detection function parameters
Scale Coefficients:  
                             estimate         se
(Intercept)              4.808522e+00 0.01779600
CovYear2007             -4.505052e-02 0.01769780
CovYear2008              3.126917e-05 0.01672416
CovYear2009             -2.788492e-02 0.01730829
CovYear2010             -6.027711e-02 0.01750727
CovYear2011             -6.886346e-02 0.01771762
CovYear2012              5.041301e-02 0.01653609
CovYear2013              3.691309e-02 0.01532418
zoneBARROIS Nord A5      2.729469e-02 0.01283388
zoneSARCE plaine Seine   2.877689e-02 0.01157661
zoneSARCE plateau côtes -2.160973e-02 0.01295866


Adjustment term parameter(s):  
                 estimate          se
herm, order 4 -0.06742156 0.002012472


As in the example from Buckland et al. book (2015 Distance sampling: methods and application) using the Hawaiian amaihi case study, i would like to be able to plot the detection function depending on the year and the site.
However,I have some difficulties to retrieve the  
Because it could have been a little bit complicated, I tried to do it first with the same model without covariates:
final_nocov <- ds(dataDS,transect="point",formula=~1,
           key="hn",adjustment="herm",order=2,convert.units=0.001)

From my understanding of the detection function, I should be able to retrieve the equation based on 
g(y)= key(y)*[1+series(y)],
with key = exp(-y^2/(2*sigma^2)) 
and serie = a*H(y/sigma). 
Following the code of the mrds package (hermite.poly.R), I used the equation available here to compute the hermite polynomial equation. With order = 2 given in ds, the hermite polynomial is of order 4. Thus, H4(x) = 16*x^4-48x^2+12

Thus, I write the following code to plot the detection function:
g.herm <- function(y,sigma,a){
  x <- y/sigma
  exp(-y^2/(2*sigma^2))*(1+a*(16*x^4-48*x^2+12))  ## this need to be confirmed
}
final_nocov.df <- g.herm(1:600,sigma=exp(final_nocov$ddf$par[1]),a=final_nocov$ddf$par[2])

When I plot both my function and the fitted model, one can easily see that there is a problem ... 

Could someoen correct me about the use of the expansion series to retrieve the correct equation of the detection function.

Thanks for your help,
Cheers,

Guillaume

messages.author: 3c8299ac8234f5d2
messages.subject: Re: replot detection function in MCDS
parts:
Guillaume,

I recently encountered a similar challenge where I wanted to re-create my own detection function plots in R.

You might want to inspect the mrds:::detfct function, and extract the code that is relevant to your example.
I think your issue may (in part at least) be due to a lack of scaling of the detection function.

Below is a short script I put together to plot a hazard-rate model with one factor variable.
It did not (admittedly) include an expansion series, but it should hopefully put you on the right track (especially if you look at mrds:::detfct).


# Scaling factor needed for correct plotting
# From mrds:::scalevalue
scale.value<-function (key.scale, z) 
{exp(as.matrix(z) %*% key.scale)}

# This function calculates the detection probability according to a hazard rate model
# from mrds:::keyfct.hz
key.fct.hz<-function (distance, key.scale, key.shape) 
{ return(1 - exp(-(distance/key.scale)^(-key.shape)))}

# Vector of distances used to re-create the detection function (from 0 out to truncation distance of 250 m)
distances<-seq(0,250,length.out = 100)

# Using a hazard-rate model with one (dichotomous, 1/0) factor variable that only affects the scale
# (not the shape) of the detection function:

# Shape parameter
key.shape<-scale.value(model$ddf$ds$aux$ddfobj$shape$parameters, 
                       matrix(1,nrow = 100,1))

# Scale parameter
# Factor = 0
mat0<-matrix(1,nrow = 100,ncol = 2)
mat0[,2]<-0
key.scale0<-scale.value(model$ddf$ds$aux$ddfobj$scale$parameters,mat0)

# Factor = 1
mat1<-matrix(1,nrow = 100,ncol = 2)
key.scale1<-scale.value(model$ddf$ds$aux$ddfobj$scale$parameters,mat1)

# Calculate detection probability values
y.val0<- key.fct.hz(distances, key.scale0, key.shape)
y.val1<- key.fct.hz(distances, key.scale1, key.shape)

# Now let's re-create the histogram
# from mrds:::detfct
bindata <- function(x, r, breaks) {
  return(hist(r[r >= x[1] & r <= x[2]], breaks = breaks, 
              plot = FALSE)$counts)}
sumit <- function(x, n, wt) {
  return(sum(x/(wt * n)))}
selected <- rep(TRUE, nrow(model$ddf$ds$aux$ddfobj$xmat))

# Detection probability for each fitted value & Nhat estimate
if (length(model$ddf$fitted) == 1) {
  pdot <- rep(model$ddf$fitted, sum(as.numeric(selected)))
}else {
  pdot <- model$ddf$fitted[selected]
  Nhat <- sum(1/pdot)
}

# Create a dummy histogram (h1)
# dist.data is the data.frame object of the distance data
# Right-truncating here at 250 m
# If you inspect the internal functions of the mrds package, you will find how the number of histogram breaks is calculated. In my case, the value is 11
h1<-hist(dist.data[dist.data$distance<=250,]$distance, breaks=seq(0,250,250/11))

# Calculate expected counts for each distance value
expected.counts <- apply(t(as.matrix(c(0,250))), 1, bindata, r = (0:1000) * 250/1001, breaks = seq(0,250,250/11))
expected.counts <- apply(expected.counts, 1, sumit, n = 1001, wt = pdot)

# Re-scale the counts
h1$counts<-h1$counts/expected.counts

# Use the ggplot2 package to plot the histogram (as rectangles) and overlay the detection function
# plotting options
gg.opts <- theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),
                 panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
                 panel.background=element_blank())

ggplot() + 
  geom_rect(aes(xmin=x[1:length(x)-1], xmax=x[2:length(x)], ymin=rep(0,length(x)-1),ymax=h1$counts), fill="white", color="black")+ 
  geom_line(data=data.frame(x=distances, y=y.val0), aes(x=x, y=y))+ # Factor level 0
  geom_line(data=data.frame(x=distances, y=y.val1), aes(x=x, y=y), linetype="dashed")+ # Factor level 1
  gg.opts+
  xlab("Distance (m)")+
  ylab("Detection probability")



Hope this helps.
Phil

messages.subject: Re: replot detection function in MCDS
parts:
Hi Phil,

Thanks for your answer. It seems to be one of the clues for my problem.
Indeed, I have always the feeling that something is not exactly on the right scale ...

First, I solved aprt of my problem: I had looked at the mrds function to see how the expansion series were built. I found that the function returns the exp(adj.series) to ensure that g(y)>0. 

> mrds:::adjfct.herm

adjfct.herm <-
       function(distance,scaling=1,adj.order,adj.parm=NULL,adj.exp=FALSE)
#
# adjfct.herm
#
# Hermite polynomial adjustment terms
#
#
# Arguments:
#
# distance  - perpendicular distance vector
# scaling     - scale parameter
# adj.order - vector of orders of polynomials to fit
# adj.parm  - vector of parameters (a_j)
#
{
# Check the adjustment parameters
 if(is.null(adj.parm)){
         adj.parm <- as.vector(rep(1,length(adj.order)))
}
     
        adj.order <- as.vector(adj.order)
     
        hermsum <- 0
   
       for(i in 1:length(adj.order))
          hermsum <- hermsum + (adj.parm[i]*hermite.poly((distance/scaling),adj.order[i]))
#   if adj.exp return exp(hermsum) to keep f(x)>0      
        if(adj.exp)
            return(exp(hermsum))
   else
           return(hermsum)
}



My problem is not yet solved but one can see the difference.


Now, this scale function seems very important. 
Will look at it, try something and I hope to find the final issue !

Thanks again !

Guillaume

parts:
Guillaume

When working with point transects and when including covariates in the detection function, plotting is a challenge.  A recent (19 Nov) change to a function in the mrds() package on Github but not yet on CRAN, is intended to make that easier.

Bring the latest version of mrds() from Github

devtools:::install_github("DistanceDevelopment", mrds)

Have a look at plot.ds() that uses a ddf object as argument, along with "pdf=TRUE" to get a plot that is useful for point transect data.

Let us know if that gets you further along.

# If you inspect the internal functions of the mrds package, you will find how the number of histogram breaks is calculated. In my case, the value is 11
h1<-hist(dist.data[dist.data$distance<=250,]$distance, breaks=seq(0,250,250/11))

# Calculate expected counts for each distance value
expected.counts <- apply(t(as.matrix(c(0,250))), 1, bindata, r = (0:1000) * 250/1001, breaks = seq(0,250,250/11))
expected.counts <- apply(expected.counts, 1, sumit, n = 1001, wt = pdot)

# Re-scale the counts
h1$counts<-h1$counts/expected.counts

# Use the ggplot2 package to plot the histogram (as rectangles) and overlay the detection function
# plotting options
gg.opts <- theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),
                 panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
                 panel.background=element_blank())

ggplot() + 
  geom_rect(aes(xmin=x[1:length(x)-1], xmax=x[2:length(x)], ymin=rep(0,length(x)-1),ymax=h1$counts), fill="white", color="black")+ 
  geom_line(data=data.frame(x=distances, y=y.val0), aes(x=x, y=y))+ # Factor level 0
  geom_line(data=data.frame(x=distances, y=y.val1), aes(x=x, y=y), linetype="dashed")+ # Factor level 1
  gg.opts+
  xlab("Distance (m)")+
  ylab("Detection probability")



Hope this helps.
Phil

Dear Eric, Philippe and all list-users,

Sorry for a late reply, but I had to manage other projects since last time.

With Eric help, I have been able to compute the detection probability for hares using the half-normal key function with hermite polynomial and also covariates (years and area).

Here is the code I used and the final plot for year 2006 : 
final$ddf$par
# Intercept[1]          CovYear2007[2]          CovYear2008[3]          CovYear2009[4]          CovYear2010[5]
# 5.163597494            -0.077848472            -0.003582774            -0.048619934            -0.103227843
# CovYear2011[6]        CovYear2012[7]          CovYear2013[8]     zoneBARROIS.Nord.A5[9]  zoneSARCE.plaine.Seine[10]
# -0.118052539             0.089956855             0.063322206             0.048347985             0.050961822
# zoneSARCE.plateau.côtes[11]       herm[12]
# -0.034803549                  0.051477479
# half-normal + hermite polynomial (order 4) + Covyear + Zone
g.herm.cov <- function(y,param,w,an07,an08,an09,an10,an11,an12,an13,barN,sarPla,sarCo){
  param <- unname(param)
  nu      <- param[1] + an07*param[2] + an08*param[3] + an09*param[4] + an10*param[5] + an11*param[6] + an12*param[7] + an13*param[8] + barN*param[9] + sarPla*param[10] + sarCo*param[11]
  sigma   <- exp(nu)
  x       <- y/w
  key     <- exp(-y^2/(2*sigma^2))
  key0    <- exp(-(0)^2/(2*sigma^2))
  serie   <- 1+exp(param[12]*(x^4-6*x^2+3))  # following Distance 7.0 User's manual p.101, Hermite polynomial of order 4 is : x^4-6*x^2+3
  serie0  <- 1+exp(param[12]*(0^4-6*0^2+3))
  pdet    <- key*(1+serie)/(key0*(1+serie0))
  return(pdet)
}
dist <- seq(0,600,0.5)
Barrois.Sud  <- g.herm.cov(dist,final$ddf$par,final$ddf$ds$aux$width,an07=0,an08=0,an09=0,an10=0,an11=0,an12=0,an13=0,barN=0,sarPla=0,sarCo=0)
Barrois.nord <- g.herm.cov(dist,final$ddf$par,final$ddf$ds$aux$width,an07=0,an08=0,an09=0,an10=0,an11=0,an12=0,an13=0,barN=1,sarPla=0,sarCo=0)
Sarce.Plaine <- g.herm.cov(dist,final$ddf$par,final$ddf$ds$aux$width,an07=0,an08=0,an09=0,an10=0,an11=0,an12=0,an13=0,barN=0,sarPla=1,sarCo=0)
sarce.Cotes  <- g.herm.cov(dist,final$ddf$par,final$ddf$ds$aux$width,an07=0,an08=0,an09=0,an10=0,an11=0,an12=0,an13=0,barN=0,sarPla=0,sarCo=1)

plot(dist,Barrois.Sud,type="n",main = "Hares detection in 2006 \n HalfNorm + Herm^4",
     ylab="Detection probability",xlab = "Distance")
lines(dist,Barrois.Sud,type="l",col="red",lty=3,lwd=2)
lines(dist,Barrois.nord,col="orange",lty=1,lwd=2)
lines(dist,Sarce.Plaine,col="blue",lty=3,lwd=2)
lines(dist,sarce.Cotes,col="green",lty=1,lwd=2)
legend("topright",legend = c("Barrois Sud","Barrois Nord","Sarce Plaine","Sarce Côtes"),
       col=c("red","orange","blue","green"),lty = c(3,1,3,1),lwd = 2, title = "Zone")

lines(dist,sarce.Cotes,col="green",lty=1,lwd=2)
legend("topright",legend = c("Barrois Sud","Barrois Nord","Sarce Plaine","Sarce Côtes"),
       col=c("red","orange","blue","green"),lty = c(3,1,3,1),lwd = 2, title = "Zone")


Thanks again for the help.
Cheers,

Guillaume
